title: Dispatch: Compare the canonical revocation position in the scheduled-successor guard (closure pass F2 bypass)
description:
Bounded follow-up to eshyra-jhpt.rev15 (merged at 8e9d77d). Supervisor probe at 8e9d77d found that the new F2 store guard in revokeCampaignRule compares input.revokedPosition (the caller's RAW anchor) against existing.effectivePosition BEFORE canonicalization. Because the __future__ anchor sorts before any real anchor at the same ordinal, a caller can bypass the guard by supplying the successor's effective ordinal with fabricated session/turn ids.

REPRO at 8e9d77d: A effective 1; ten committed turns; supersede A with B effective 15 (stored future(15)); revokeCampaignRule(B, revokedPosition {s, t15, 15}) -> ACCEPTED, stored revokedPosition = {__future__, __future__, 15} == B.effectivePosition; active sets: 14 = [A], 15 = [], 20 = []; validateCampaignRules(listCampaignRules) -> THROWS "successor 'B' of 'A' was revoked before taking effect". So the store produced a history the validator rejects — the exact store/validator mismatch class this closure pass exists to remove. (Revoking at 11 is correctly rejected; only the same-ordinal path leaks.)

WORKTREE / BRANCH: .worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev16 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev16, cut from eshyra-jhpt at 8e9d77d. npm ci already run.

FIX: in revokeCampaignRule, validate/format input.revokedPosition and compute the canonical revokedPosition (canonicalizeFuturePosition) FIRST, then run the strict-prospectivity guard and the scheduled-successor guard against the CANONICAL position (compareCampaignPositions(canonical, existing.effectivePosition) <= 0). Keep messages unchanged. Also assert the reverse direction in the same function: after the write, the persisted rule must satisfy the validator's mirror (revokedPosition > effectivePosition whenever a prior names it) — a cheap self-check is acceptable but not required; say which you chose.

EVIDENCE (must FAIL against 8e9d77d): extend campaignRuleLifecycleMatrix.test.ts X2 with the same-ordinal fabricated-anchor case: revocation at {fabricated ids, ordinal == B.effective ordinal} is rejected with the F2 message; rows and active sets unchanged; validateCampaignRules(listCampaignRules) still accepts the pre-revocation history. Also add the positive boundary: revocation at ordinal B.effective+1 is accepted, B active exactly at B.effective, and the history validates.

VERIFICATION: npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing; report pass/skip counts and confirm worktree-local resolution. Change nothing else.
